name: Jumada al-Thani
intro:
The month of Jumada al-Thani holds days of sorrow and joy together. The days 3, 4, 12, 13, 19, 20, 21, 22, 27, 28 and 29 are the days on which these reports can be found. The martyrdom of Lady Zahra (SA), the passing of Lady Umm Kulthum (SA), the passing of Lady Umm al-Banin (SA), the martyrdom of Sultan Ali ibn Muhammad al-Baqir (PBUH), the passing of Sayyid Muhammad ibn Ali al-Hadi (PBUH), and the martyrdom of Ibrahim ibn Malik al-Ashtar are the sorrowful events of this month.
The wedding day of the parents of the Prophet (SAWW), Abdullah and Amina (PBUT), the entrusting of the Prophet (SAWW) to Halima al-Sa'diyya, the birth of Lady Zahra (SA), the death of Abu Bakr, and the death of Harun al-Rashid are the joyful events of this month.

events.title: Martyrdom of Lady Zahra (SA)
events.text:
Imam Reza (PBUH) said: “Inna Fatimata siddiqatun shahidah” — “Indeed, Fatima is truthful and a martyr.”
On this day in the year 11 AH, according to the account of 95 days, on a Tuesday, the martyrdom of Lady Batul, the Virgin, the oppressed and beaten one, the Mistress of the Women, Fatima Zahra (SA), took place.
After the martyrdom and burial of the Prophet (SAWW), they stormed the house of Amir al-Mu'minin and Fatima Zahra (PBUT) three times, and each time they committed some form of disrespect against the Ahl al-Bayt (PBUT). On one of these occasions, when they set fire to the house and forced their way in, Lady Siddiqa (SA) was standing behind the door.
Although he knew she was behind the door, he kicked and pushed it open, and the nail of the door pierced the chest of that noble lady, Muhsin (PBUH) was miscarried, and she lay unconscious on the ground on her side; and they took Mawla al-Muwahhidin (PBUH) toward the mosque, bareheaded and barefoot, with his hands bound.
When Lady Zahra (SA) regained consciousness, she followed Amir al-Mu'minin (PBUH) and prevented them from taking him to the mosque. In the alley, before the eyes of her husband, Asadullah al-Ghalib, Amir al-Mu'minin Ali ibn Abi Talib (PBUT), they struck the body of Lady Siddiqa the Martyr (SA) with a whip and the sheath of a sword, so that, according to some narrations, blood flowed from her arm, and she again fell unconscious on the ground.
sources: A'lam al-Wara: vol. 1, p. 300. Kashf al-Ghumma: vol. 1, p. 503. Masar al-Shi'a: p. 31. Tawdih al-Maqasid: p. 13. Misbah al-Kaf'ami: vol. 2, p. 597. Misbah al-Mutahajjid: p. 732. Bihar al-Anwar: vol. 97, p. 375; vol. 43, p. 195.
Usul al-Kafi: vol. 3, p. 475.
Mustadrak Safinat al-Bihar: vol. 2, p. 85 (?)

subsections.title: The Days of Fatima's (SA) Sorrow
subsections.text:
After these events and calamities, on some days she would go, with a broken and grieving heart, to the graves of the martyrs of Uhud, weep there, and ask God for her own death. Gradually the pain and wounds of her body increased, and from then on she would sit under a tree near Medina, weeping and lamenting. The hypocrites cut down that tree as well. After that, Amir al-Mu'minin (PBUH) built a shelter for her there, which became known as the “Bayt al-Ahzan” (House of Sorrows).
Day by day the lady's illness grew more severe. Her chest broken and wounded, her arm swollen, her face bruised blue, Muhsin lost, the grief for the Prophet (SAWW), and the oppression of Amir al-Mu'minin (PBUH) brought matters to the point where she fell into her sickbed, and gave her last wishes to Amir al-Mu'minin (PBUH): “Wash me at night, in my shirt, shroud me and bury me. Let my grave be hidden, and let Abu Bakr and Umar not attend my funeral procession or my prayer.”
Medina on the Martyrdom of Fatima (SA)
On the day of her martyrdom, Medina was like the day of the martyrdom of the Seal of the Prophets (SAWW). Young and old, men and women, were all lamenting and weeping. Her pure body was washed at night, and at the time of the washing, Amir al-Mu'minin, Hasan and Husayn, Zaynab and Umm Kulthum (PBUT), Fidda the maidservant, and Asma bint Umays were present. Then a number of the finest of the companions of Amir al-Mu'minin (PBUH) — Salman, Abu Dharr, Miqdad, Ammar and others — came and buried the body.
At Baqi', they prepared forty grave-shapes and sprinkled some water over them. The next day the hypocrites intended to dig up the grave, but Amir al-Mu'minin (PBUH) did not permit it.
There are several possibilities for the place of her burial, but visiting her has been reported to be proper at the Prophet's Mosque (SAWW), at her own chamber — which in our time is part of the mosque's courtyard — between the mihrab and the minbar, and at Baqi'.
The length of the life of that oppressed lady was 18 years and 60 or 90 days. The year of her martyrdom is the eleventh year of the Hijra.
sources: Bayt al-Ahzan: pp. 247–262. Bihar al-Anwar: vol. 43, p. 171. Fayd al-Alam: pp. 258–263. Jannat al-Asima: pp. 351–361. Riyahin al-Shari'a: vol. 1, pp. 251–293. subsections.title: Accounts of the Date of the Martyrdom of Lady Zahra (SA)
subsections.text:
The accounts regarding the martyrdom of Lady Zahra (SA) are as follows:
1. Forty days after the martyrdom of the Prophet (SAWW) (Rabi' al-Thani).
2. Forty-five days (the thirteenth of Rabi' al-Thani).
3. Sixty days after the martyrdom of the Prophet (SAWW).
4. Seventy-two days after the martyrdom of the Prophet (SAWW).
5. Seventy-five days after the martyrdom of the Prophet (SAWW).
6. Ninety days after the martyrdom of the Prophet (SAWW).
7. Ninety-five days after the martyrdom of the Prophet (SAWW) (the third of Jumada al-Akhir).
8. One hundred days after the martyrdom of the Prophet (SAWW) (the eighth of Jumada al-Akhir).
9. One hundred and twelve days after the martyrdom of the Prophet (SAWW) (the 20th of Jumada al-Akhir).
10. Four months after the martyrdom of the Prophet (SAWW).
11. The 21st of Rajab.
12. The 25th of Rajab.
13. The third of the month of Ramadan.
14. Eight months after the martyrdom of the Prophet (SAWW).
Regarding the martyrdom of Lady Zahra (SA), it is fitting to review the relevant sources.

Ithbat al-Hudat: vol. 1, pp. 280–281. Irshad al-Qulub by al-Daylami: p. 295. Al-Muhtadar: p. 109. Amali of al-Saduq: pp. 99, 101, 118. Manaqib of Ibn Shahrashub: vol. 2, p. 209. For the slap and the bruised eye of that lady, refer to these books:
Sirat al-A'imma al-Ithna Ashar: vol. 1, p. 132. Ma'sat al-Zahra: vol. 1, pp. 164–193. Al-Asrar al-Fatimiyya: p. 135.
For the cause of the martyrdom of Muhsin (PBUH), refer to these books:
Ithbat al-Wasiyya: p. 143. Al-Wafi bi al-Wafayat: vol. 6, p. 17. Tarajim A'lam al-Nisa: vol. 2, p. 317. Fara'id al-Simtayn: vol. 2, pp. 34–35. Amali of al-Saduq: pp. 99–101. Bisharat al-Mustafa: pp. 197–200.
As for the fact that she was martyred and did not pass away by natural death, the statement of Imam Reza (PBUH) is sufficient, who said: “Innaha siddiqatun shahidah”... “Indeed Fatima (SA) is truthful and a martyr.” Refer also to the following sources:
Mazar of Shaykh al-Mufid: p. 156. Muqni'a of Shaykh al-Mufid: p. 459. Balad al-Amin: pp. 198–278. Therefore, on this day the Shi'a should rise up to mourn her, visit that oppressed lady, and curse the oppressors and usurpers of her right.

events.title: Death of Harun al-Rashid
events.text: On the night of the fourth, in the year 193 AH, the wretched and vile Harun al-Rashid, at the age of 45, went to his reckoning in hell. He ruled as caliph for 23 years, and his grave lies behind that of Imam Reza (PBUH); it is fitting for those who visit to curse Harun.
sources: Tawdih al-Maqasid: p. 13.

events.title: Departure Toward Khaybar
events.text: On this day in the seventh year of the Hijra, the Prophet (SAWW) set out toward Khaybar with 400 men.
sources: Waqa'i' al-Shuhur: p. 107.

events.title: Passing of Lady Umm al-Banin (SA)
events.text:
On this day in the year 64 AH, Lady Umm al-Banin (SA), the wife of Amir al-Mu'minin (PBUH) and mother of Qamar Bani Hashim (PBUH), passed away.
Her blessed name was Fatima, and her honorific title is Umm al-Banin; she is known by this title. Her father was Hizam ibn Khalid, and her mother was Layla, daughter of Shahid ibn Abi Amir.
Amir al-Mu'minin chose her as his wife, and God granted her four sons: Qamar Bani Hashim Abbas (PBUH), Abdullah, Ja'far and Uthman (PBUT), all four of whom were martyred in Karbala.
The women who returned from Karbala to Medina would hold mourning gatherings at the house of Umm al-Banin (SA). Although she had not been in Karbala, she had no rest from lamenting and weeping, and every day she would go to Baqi' and recite elegies so heart-rending that even Marwan, with all his hardness of heart, would weep. When the women addressed her as Umm al-Banin and offered condolences, she would say: “Do not call me Umm al-Banin any more...”
This weeping and lamentation of hers continued until she bade farewell to life.
sources: Umm al-Banin (SA), Sayyidat Nisa al-Arab: p. 84.
Riyahin al-Shari'a: vol. 3, p. 294.

events.title: Marriage of Abdullah and Amina (PBUT)
events.text: This is the day of the marriage of Abdullah and Amina (PBUT), and of her conceiving the Messenger of God (SAWW). It is fitting for the faithful to honor and revere that night and to keep it alive with worship.
sources: Tuhfat al-Za'ir: pp. 56–57. Fayd al-Alam: p. 272.
Fayd al-Alam: p. 272.

events.title: Birth of Lady Zahra (SA)
events.text:
On such a day, Lady Hawra' Insiyya, the Virgin, Batul, Umm Abiha, Lady Fatima Zahra (SA), was born in Mecca in the fifth year of the Prophetic mission. According to one account, her birth was on the tenth of Jumada al-Akhir.
The Conception of Fatima (SA)
The story of the conception of Lady Fatima Zahra (SA) has several stages, a summary of which follows:
1. On the Night of the Ascension (Mi'raj), God gave the Prophet (SAWW) an apple as a gift, at whose grandeur of creation, fragrance, color and beauty the angels marveled. God commanded the Prophet (SAWW) to eat it. When he split the apple, a light shone from it. Gabriel said: Eat, O Messenger of God, for this is the light of Fatima, the aided one, a daughter who will come forth from your loins. In some narrations, the Seal of the Prophets (SAWW) also ate from the dates of Paradise.
2. On the 10th of Sha'ban in the fourth year, Gabriel (PBUH) descended upon the Prophet (SAWW) at Abtah and conveyed the command to withdraw from Lady Khadija (SA) for a period of 40 days — as a preparation for the conception of Lady Zahra (SA).
Although he was deeply fond of Khadija (SA) and this was hard for him, he sent word to Khadija (SA) that he would not come home for a while and would go to the house of Fatima bint Asad (SA): “At night, lock the door and rest in your bed.”
The Prophet (SAWW) would come to the house of Fatima bint Asad (SA) at night. Every night at the time of breaking the fast, dates, grapes and heavenly food were brought. With heavenly water and a towel they would wash and clean his hands. Amir al-Mu'minin (PBUH), by the command of the Prophet (SAWW), would sit in front of the door so that no one would come in and share in that food with the Prophet (SAWW). On the fortieth night the command came: go to the house of Khadija (SA), for God has sworn by Himself that tonight He will create from your loins a pure and good offspring. He rose and came to the house of Khadija (SA).
Lady Khadija (SA) said: By the One who raised the sky and made water gush from the earth, he had not yet gone far from me when I felt the weight of Fatima (SA) within me.
The Pregnancy of Khadija (SA)
While Lady Khadija (SA) was going through her pregnancy, Lady Fatima (SA) would speak to her mother from inside the womb, console her, and call her to patience and steadfastness.
The Prophet (SAWW) said to Khadija (SA): “Gabriel gave me the good news that this child is a girl, and that she is a pure and blessed being; the Most High God will make my line and progeny through her, and from her line He will place Imams in the community who, after the end of revelation, will be his successors on earth.”
When the signs of labor appeared, she sent for the women of Quraysh, but no one came to help, because they had not approved of the marriage of Lady Khadija (SA) to the Prophet (SAWW), and Khadija (SA) was saddened by their treatment.
Just then four tall women, resembling the women of Bani Hashim, came in to her. One of them said to her: O Khadija, do not be sad, for we are messengers of your Lord. We are your sisters; I am Sarah, and this is Asiya, daughter of Muzahim, your companion in Paradise, and this is Maryam, daughter of Imran, and this is Safura, daughter of Shu'ayb. God has sent us to you to help you with the matters related to women. One of them sat on her right, another on her left, a third in front of her, and the fourth behind her.
Fatima (SA) Was Born
The exalted lady Khadija (SA) set Lady Fatima Zahra (SA), clean and pure, upon the ground. At that moment a light shone from her being that lit up all the houses of Mecca, and this light shone in the east and the west. The lady who was in front of Khadija (SA) took Lady Fatima (SA), washed her with water of Kawthar, and brought out two white cloths that were whiter than milk and more fragrant than musk and ambergris. She wrapped one around her body and placed the other over her head, and then asked her to speak.
Lady Fatima (SA) opened her lips and said: Ashhadu an la ilaha illa Allah, wa anna abi rasulu Allah sayyidu al-anbiya', wa anna ba'li sayyidu al-awsiya', wa anna waladi sayyidu al-asbat: “I bear witness that there is no god but God, that my father is the Messenger of God and the master of the prophets, that my husband is the master of the successors, and that my children are the masters of the grandchildren and tribes.”
Then she greeted each of them and called each by name. They smiled at her face, and the houris and the people of Paradise gave one another the good news of the birth of Lady Fatima (SA). A radiant light appeared in the sky, such as the angels had never seen until that day, and so they named her “Zahra” (the Radiant). The lady who was sitting in front of Khadija (SA) said to Khadija (SA): “Take her, pure and clean, adorned and blessed, for blessing has been placed in her line and progeny.”
Khadija (SA) took her from her hand with joy and contentment, placed her breast in her mouth and filled her mouth with milk, and this is how Fatima (SA) began her physical growth.

events.title: Passing of Lady Umm Kulthum (SA)
events.text:
Lady Umm Kulthum (SA) passed away four months after returning from Karbala to Medina. Her father was Mawla al-Muwahhidin Amir al-Mu'minin (PBUH), and her mother was Lady Zahra al-Mardiyya (SA).
The author of Riyahin al-Shari'a, quoting A'yan al-Shi'a, says: Amir al-Mu'minin (PBUH) married that lady to Awn ibn Ja'far al-Tayyar.
Whatever has been reported about the marriage of Umm Kulthum (SA) to anyone other than Awn ibn Ja'far is a fabrication of the opponents. She was present in the heart-rending event of Karbala, and after the martyrdom of Imam Husayn (PBUH), the Ahl al-Bayt and their companions, she stood beside her sister Lady Zaynab (SA) and protected the women and orphans; her poems of mourning for her brother in Karbala are famous and heart-rending.
After Ashura, when the women were taken captive to Kufa and Syria, her sermon in the city of Kufa and in the assembly of Ibn Ziyad, her poems at Qadisiyya and Qinnasrin, the effect of her prayer at Sibur and Baalbek, her words to Shimr at the entrance to the gate of Syria, and her elegies at Arba'in and on the return to Medina, all point to the greatness, courage and patience of that lady.
Finally, four months after entering Medina, with a heart full of grief and sorrow over the calamities of Karbala, especially the martyrdom of Sayyid al-Shuhada (PBUH), she passed away and was buried in Medina. According to one account, her passing was at the end of the month of Jumada al-Thani.
sources: Waqa'i' al-Shuhur: p. 110.

events.title: Death of Abu Bakr
events.text:
On the night of Tuesday, the 22nd of Jumada al-Thani in the year 13 AH, Abdullah ibn Uthman, known as Abu Bakr ibn Abi Quhafa, at the age of 67, departed this world toward the recompense of his deeds. According to one account, the death of Abu Bakr was on the 27th of Jumada al-Thani.
He was a usurper of the caliphate for two years, three months and twenty-two days, and he was the first to become caliph, after the martyrdom of the Prophet (SAWW), by the choice of the members of the Saqifa of Banu Sa'ida. The choosing of Abu Bakr was so haphazard that Umar, although he himself was the manager of the Saqifa affair, says: “The pledge of allegiance to Abu Bakr was a matter without forethought, consultation or care, like in the time of ignorance (Jahiliyya), and God protected the Muslims from its evil. Whoever repeats such an act, kill him.”
The Sunnis have written about the cause of his death: Abu Bakr had performed a ritual bath on Monday, the 7th of Jumada al-Akhir, and that day was cold. For this reason he caught a chill and developed a fever; this fever lasted 15 days, and he did not go to the prayer, until on the night of Tuesday, the 22nd of Jumada al-Akhir, after handing the caliphate over to Umar, he died.
Before his death he summoned Uthman to write a testament about the caliphate, stating that the caliphate after Abu Bakr should be with Umar ibn al-Khattab. He said a word and lost consciousness, and the rest Uthman wrote on his own, that the caliphate is with Umar. Abu Bakr regained consciousness and prayed for Uthman, saying that he had written what he had wanted.
One must ask: why, when the Prophet (SAWW) in the last days of his life asked for paper and pen so as to designate, by God's command, his successor after himself, did they attribute delirium to that exalted station?
At the time of his death Abu Bakr spoke some words. Among them: “I wish I had not searched the house of Fatima and Ali (PBUT).” Is this the same search that brought about the martyrdom of the piece of the Prophet's (SAWW) body?

events.title: Martyrdom of Sultan Ali ibn Muhammad al-Baqir (PBUH)
events.text:
On this day in the year 116 AH, Abu al-Hasan Sultan Ali, the son of Imam Baqir (PBUH), was martyred in Ardahal, Kashan.
A number of the friends of the Ahl al-Bayt (PBUT) from the people of Chihil Hisar and Fin of Kashan wrote a letter to Imam Baqir (PBUH), saying that since they were far from his presence, he should send one of his sons to them for their guidance and training and for teaching them the rulings of religion.
The Imam sent his noble son, Ali ibn Muhammad (PBUH), with messengers toward Kashan; and his brother Imam Sadiq (PBUH) arranged the provisions for his journey.
When he arrived, about 6,000 people came out in Fin to welcome him. For a time he was occupied with guiding the people in Jasb and Khawa, and he spent most of his time in worship in the Jami' Mosque of Kashan — which is now located in the Kuy-e Meydan-e Kohneh quarter — and the Shi'a would come into his presence to perform the Friday prayer, and they witnessed many miracles.
He would send letters to his noble father in Medina describing his own state and that of the Shi'a, until in the year 144 AH the news of the martyrdom of his noble father reached him, and three years after the martyrdom of his noble father, in the year 116 AH, his opponents martyred him together with a number of his friends, followers and those connected to him.
Since the 27th of Jumada al-Thani, in the year of his martyrdom, coincided with the 17th of Mehr in the solar calendar, every year on the second Friday of Mehr, on the occasion of his anniversary, the carpet-washing ceremony (Qali-shuyan) is held together with magnificent mourning beside his purified grave.
Now, in the crypt beneath his sacred shrine, the blessed bodies of about a hundred of those great martyrs are fresh and intact, as was witnessed by the late Ayatollah Sayyid Shihab al-Din Mar'ashi Najafi.
sources: Sharh-e Zindegani-ye Hazrat-e Sultan Ali ibn Muhammad Baqir (PBUH): p. 62. Maraqid al-Ma'arif: vol. 2, pp. 79–82. Rawdat al-Jannat: vol. 4, p. 212.
Maraqid al-Ma'arif: vol. 2, p. 80.
Refer to the book “Nur-e Bahir” by the late Baqir Marandi — and to Ajsad-e Javidan, quoting those who accompanied Ayatollah Mar'ashi Najafi in visiting the purified bodies.

events.title: Entrusting the Prophet (SAWW) to Halima al-Sa'diyya
events.text: On this day Abd al-Muttalib (PBUH) had the light of his eye, the Prophet, circumambulate the Ka'ba, and entrusted him to Halima al-Sa'diyya to be nursed.
sources: Waqa'i' al-Shuhur: p. 113.

events.title: Passing of Sayyid Muhammad, Son of Imam Hadi (PBUH)
events.text:
Sayyid Muhammad, the son of Imam Hadi (PBUH), passed away in Samarra in the year 252 AH.
He was also called Abu Ja'far, Abu Ali, and Sayyid Muhammad Ba'aj.
His rank and standing were such that some of the Shi'a thought that, after Imam Hadi (PBUH), this noble figure would be the Imam, but with his passing during the lifetime of his noble father, it became clear to all that Imam Hasan al-Askari (PBUH) was the Imam after him.
Imam Askari (PBUH) was extremely fond of Sayyid Muhammad (PBUH), to the point that at the time of his passing he tore the collar of his garment. After his passing, they buried him in a village called Balad, six farsakhs from Samarra, where his grave is now well known.
Many miracles have been witnessed from him, and it now has a dome, a courtyard and numerous chambers, and the friends of the Ahl al-Bayt (PBUT) go to visit that noble figure. The lineage of the Sadat of the Al Ba'aj in Iraq and Khuzestan goes back to Ali and Ahmad, the sons of Sayyid Muhammad Ba'aj.
sources: Maraqid al-Ma'arif: vol. 2, p. 262.
This date is well known among the Shi'a of Samarra and is also written in his shrine.

events.title: Martyrdom of Ibrahim ibn Malik al-Ashtar
events.text: In this month in the year 71 AH, Ibrahim, the son of Malik al-Ashtar al-Nakha'i (RH), was martyred.
sources: Maraqid al-Ma'arif: vol. 1, p. 37

honorifics.(SAWW): Sallallahu Alayhi wa Alihi wa Sallam — peace and blessings of Allah be upon him and his progeny (the Prophet Muhammad)
honorifics.(PBUH): Peace Be Upon Him (used for Imams, Prophets and other holy figures, male)
honorifics.(SA): Salamullah Alayha — peace be upon her (Lady Fatima, Lady Umm Kulthum, Lady Zaynab, Lady Narjis, etc.)
honorifics.(PBUT): Peace Be Upon Them (plural, e.g. the Ahl al-Bayt / the Infallible Imams)
honorifics.(ATFS): Ajjalallahu Ta'ala Farajahu ash-Sharif — may Allah hasten his noble reappearance (the Imam of the Age)
honorifics.(RA): Rahimahullah — may Allah have mercy on him
